evidence.note: At step 4000 diagnosed the 30.6M model would plateau above target (extrapolated slowing improvement), then made a targeted design change — scaled to 53.8M params with mixed q4/q8 checkpointing specifically to stay under the byte cap. Capacity-vs-size reasoning, not a blind retry.

Explicitly diagnosed the binding constraint: loaded q4 checkpoint validated at 1.008 vs full-precision 0.970, identifying ~0.10 nats of quantization loss as the real problem — the core capacity-vs-quant-loss discrimination the anchor-8 level calls for.

Adapted the design to the diagnosis: fine-tuned from the quantized model and switched q4→q5; then detected q5 overshot the 32MB cap (33.5MB) and pivoted to a mixed q5/q4 scheme — trading quantization scheme against size.

Treated the size↔quant↔bpb frontier as the object of optimization, iterating over many quantization policies (layer-subset q4/q5, embedding q5/q6/q7, NF4, lzma, hybrid qmix) plus quant-aware fine-tuning. Each falsified run updated the policy choice — but the search was scattershot with strong diminishing returns.

Weakness: sank substantial compute into a long unproductive quant search it could not interrupt (repeated failed Ctrl+C), rather than abandoning the dead end early — keeps it below the level-10 'compounding, headroom, early abandonment' bar.

reasoning: The agent repeatedly diagnosed the binding constraint from evidence — under-capacity (step 28), then quantization loss of 0.10 nats (step 91), then byte-cap overshoot (step 95) — and adapted the design each time by trading depth/width and the quantization scheme against size to buy accuracy, exactly matching the anchor-8 description. It falls short of 10 because the late quantization search became scattershot with heavy diminishing returns, dead ends were not abandoned early (compute sunk into a search it couldn't interrupt), and it landed with a razor-thin margin rather than principled headroom.
